conviction_note: No unpriced company-level number found. The consensus bar (Q3 revenue about $247.2M, EPS about $0.03) falls inside what the company's own FY guide implies. The small positive sum comes from a 10%-of-float short, a guide-raise setup with FY consensus at the low end of the range, and an easy Q3-2025 margin comparison. A 20% five-day run-up to a 52-week high works against it. With no usable chain, p_up 54 is set on a 14% scale from the name's own median reaction (15.9%, last two prints about 6%), giving +1.1. The findings sum (+2.0) is larger than that because each finding is sized alone, and the run-up caveat sits mostly in p_up.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus about $247.2M (-8.5% y/y) and EPS about $0.03, FY2026 revenue consensus about $955M against the company's raised FY guide of net sales -3% to -5% ex-FX (about $954-974M), adjusted operating margin 4-6%, gross margin 'upper 50s', positive FCF, return to growth in Q4 (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/FOSL/22739, 2026-11-03; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/883569/000088356926000052/q22026ex991.htm, 2026-08-12). The revenue bar has one estimate source. It cross-checks against guide arithmetic: H1 reported $434.5M (224.8 + 209.7), so the FY midpoint (about $964M) with Q4 slightly up on Q4-2025's $280.5M implies Q3 of about $246-247M. The bar is effectively company-guided.
positioning_check: Short interest 5.63M shares as of the 2026-10-15 settlement, about 10% of float, 6.8 days to cover on about 829K average volume (https://massive.com/quote/fosl, page dated 2026-11-10). Stocktitan shows 5.6M, 10.0% of float, 6.8 days (https://www.stocktitan.net/overview/FOSL/). Earlier, the Sep-30 settlement was 7.4M shares / 13% of float / 10.9 days, so shorts were covering into October. Skew: not available. The chain is unusable (ATM spread 90% of mid, ATM IV 144%, put/call OI 0.85, total OI 3,134). Tape: +19.96% over 5 days, +12.2% over 20 days, 0.4% below the 52-week high, +348% off the 52-week low. Market cap about $477M on 59.1M shares.

findings.finding: FOSL rose about 20% in the five sessions into the print ($6.81 on 2026-11-03 to $8.03-8.10 on 2026-11-10) to a 52-week high, with no company news in EDGAR or the wire since the 2026-10-08 date announcement. That raises the bar above a consensus that only asks for Q3 revenue -8.5% and EPS of $0.03.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Before the Q2 print the stock jumped 19% on no news a week ahead (Barchart) and still rose +5.88% on the print with a guide raise. Q1 2026, after a run, +6.1%. 6 of 7 recent prints were up.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. The question is whether the run-up has front-run a good print. If the market were already paying for a beat-and-raise, the tape would look like this: a 20% week and the stock at a 52-week high. So the finding pulls the reaction down, not the print.
findings.independence: The Earnings Whispers preview (2026-11-03, https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/FOSL/22739) notes that sentiment turned bullish and the move raises the bar. The Barchart piece on the August pre-print jump (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3642758/fossil-stock-jumps-19-on-no-news-it-could-be-a-high-risk-high-reward-bet-for-speculators-willing-to-take-a-bite) shows the same pattern did not lead to a sell-off last time.

findings.finding: Short interest was 5.63M shares (about 10% of float, 6.8 days to cover) at the 2026-10-15 settlement, down from 7.4M / 13% / 10.9 days at the end of September. A still-sizeable short gives an upside mechanism if the Q4 return-to-growth guide is reaffirmed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prints with a positive guide surprise in 2025 (2025-08-13 +29.8%, 2025-03-12 +29.1%) came when short interest was larger. The baseline does not record short interest at those dates.
findings.why_not_priced: Part of the 20% week is likely covering (short interest fell from about 7.4M to 5.6M shares between the late-September and mid-October settlements), but 6.8 days to cover remains. A fully covered short would show days to cover near 2-3, the bottom of the 2.8-14.6 range on Stocktitan's chart.
findings.independence: Stocktitan, a different aggregator, shows the same 5.6M / 10.0% / 6.8 days (https://www.stocktitan.net/overview/FOSL/).

findings.finding: FY2026 consensus revenue (about $955M) sits at the very bottom of the raised guide ($954-974M ex-FX). On guide arithmetic that implies Q4 below Q4-2025's $280.5M (955 - 434.5 H1 - 247.2 Q3 = $273M, about -2.7%), while management says Q4 returns to growth. A reaffirmed guide plus Q4 growth makes the Street's FY number stale.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The first FY guide raise (2026-08-12) bought only +5.88%. The guide reiteration in May bought +6.1%. The Q4-2025 print with a first FY2026 guide bought +16.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: If the Street believed the Q4 growth call, FY consensus would sit near the guide midpoint (about $964M), not at $955M. The gap of about $9M is all in Q4. The 20% run-up shows that some of this is now in the price, so the size is held small.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers (2026-11-03) states FY consensus about $955M near the low end and that analysts 'aren't expecting the upper half' (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/FOSL/22739). Q1 sales $224.8M from https://www.barchart.com/story/news/1913891/fossil-group-inc-reports-first-quarter-2026-financial-results. Q4-2025 $280.5M from https://www.barchart.com/story/news/697273/fossil-group-inc-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results.

findings.finding: Peer Movado reported after Fossil last spoke (2026-08-27, quarter to July 31). Net sales rose +4.9% and US sales +4.9%, with growth across licensed fashion brands and wholesale, and Middle East tourism markets were a drag. This supports Fossil's US wholesale watch trend (Fossil-brand US wholesale traditional watches +16% in Q2).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No record of how FOSL reacts to its wholesale line specifically. Q2's wholesale +0.9% cc with a margin beat bought +5.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer's print is public, but the Q3 revenue consensus still models -8.5%, steeper than Q2's -4.9%, on regional restructuring. A peer read pointing to a firm US fashion-watch market would show up as estimates drifting up, and the bar has not moved off the guide arithmetic.
findings.independence: This is a proxy, not Fossil's own number. Fossil Q2 call: Fossil-brand wholesale traditional watches +12% globally, +16% US (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262105791-tradingkey).

findings.finding: Fossil's guide assumes no further tariff refunds in 2026. It recognised $5.9M of IEEPA refund in Q1 and collected $4.9M of it in Q2. Movado booked $3.2M of IEEPA refunds in its July quarter, and the CBP CAPE process was running, so a further refund in Q3 is possible but would be excluded from adjusted results.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 refund was excluded from adjusted results. That print bought +6.1% on the operating story.
findings.why_not_priced: A refund is not in the guide or in consensus EPS by the company's own statement. It is a one-off below adjusted operating income with no path to the guide, so it is sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: Movado refund (https://fashionunited.uk/news/business/movado-group-reports-strong-sales-and-profit-growth-in-second-quarter/2026082789994). CBP CAPE process status (https://www.strtrade.com/trade-news-resources/str-trade-report/trade-report/2026_/june_/cbp-preparing-for-more-tariff-refunds-even-as-key-issue-remains-disputed).

findings.finding: Weak EMEA is a risk to the Q4 growth call. Fossil itself flagged uncertain conditions and gas prices as risks to Q4 growth. The preview cites weaker EMEA tied to Middle East tensions and soft travel retail, and Movado named the Middle East as a drag. Europe was already -14% cc in Fossil's Q1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (2025-11-13), a sales decline with a debt exchange the same day, fell -9.05%. That is the only negative print in the last seven.
findings.why_not_priced: The EMEA weakness is partly in the -8.5% Q3 bar. The Q4 growth language has not been tested, though. If the market had priced a Q4 wobble, FY consensus would sit below the guide range, and it sits at the low end, inside it.
findings.independence: Fossil Q2 call risk language (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262105791-tradingkey). Movado Middle East drag (https://fashionunited.uk/news/business/movado-group-reports-strong-sales-and-profit-growth-in-second-quarter/2026082789994). Q1 Europe -14% (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/1913891/fossil-group-inc-reports-first-quarter-2026-financial-results).

findings.finding: Balance sheet at Q2: total debt $203.0M (up from $173.8M at year end), quarterly interest $8.3M against $4.3M a year ago, cash $79.0M against $95.8M at year end, liquidity $96.6M, H1 operating cash use $31.0M. Inventory was $177.9M, flat year on year but up from $151.8M at year end. Management still guides positive FY free cash flow, so H2 must generate more than $31M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025-11-13 print coincided with the debt exchange and fell -9%. Since then financing has not been the reaction line.
findings.why_not_priced: What does the money buy? The inventory build is seasonal and flat year on year, which fits the Q4 launch and holiday sell-in rather than a stuck build. The interest burden is known. The risk is that Q3 cash and FCF tracking against the guide disappoint. A market pricing distress would not be trading the stock at a 52-week high at 0.47x sales.
findings.independence: The 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/883569/000088356926000055/0000883569-26-000055-index.htm) is the same company document set, so it does not count as independent. Restructuring charges were $3.4M in Q2.

findings.finding: Sell-side coverage widened into the print. Craig-Hallum initiated on 2026-09-10 with a $12 target and Lake Street set $10 on 2026-10-15, against spot of about $8.03. The average target is about $9.
findings.why_not_priced: This is wire copy and largely priced. It matters only in that new small-cap coverage gives more buyers on a reaffirmed guide. Management also presents at the Craig-Hallum conference on 2026-11-17, after the window.
findings.independence: The finviz Q3 date release names the Craig-Hallum (Nov 17) and Northland (Dec 16) conferences (https://finviz.com/news/404812/fossil-group-inc-announces-date-for-third-quarter-2026-earnings-release-and-conference-call).

findings.finding: Q3 2025 is an easy profit comparison: gross margin 48.7% and adjusted EPS -$0.63 a year ago. Q2 2026 gross margin was 62.4% (+490bp) and the FY gross margin guide is 'upper 50s', which implies an H2 gross margin step-down that may prove conservative. Consensus EPS of $0.03 already embeds a large improvement.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 margin beat (+490bp) bought +5.88%. Margin beats have been bought modestly.
findings.why_not_priced: The step-down in the 'upper 50s' guide is the company's own conservatism. If the market expected a Q3 gross margin near 60%, consensus EPS would sit well above $0.03 with interest at about $8M a quarter. It sits barely above zero.
findings.independence: Fossil Q2 release, gross margin 62.4% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/883569/000088356926000052/q22026ex991.htm). FY gross margin 'upper 50s' on the Q2 call (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262105791-tradingkey).

outside_window.finding: Management presents at the Craig-Hallum Alpha Select Conference on 2026-11-17 and Northland on 2026-12-16. Follow-through buying or selling from those comes after the exit.

rejected_candidates.detail: Merged into the gross margin finding (Q3 margin and the 'upper 50s' guide). Kept apart here because Fossil has not confirmed the transmission.

baseline_tension: The baseline has no usable skew. The +20% five-day run-up to a 52-week high cuts against the mildly positive evidence, and a still-10% short and a 6-of-7-up reaction history cut the other way. On net the run-up pulls p_up toward 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (an unexplained move is worth about 0): the no-news run-up finding was cut from -1.0 to -0.3, and its weight moved into p_up
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; the last guide raise bought only +5.9%): the guidance finding was cut from +1.0 to +0.8
Lesson 2 (one-offs sized as one-offs): the tariff refund was cut from +0.3 to +0.2, lands_on one_off
Lesson 8 (size on the name's own distribution, understatement is the systematic error): abs_move_pct raised from 12 to 14 against a median of 15.9; p_up 53 to 54 after the run-up finding shrank

Lessons 4, 6, 7 left the rest standing: financing was asked what it buys (seasonal, flat y/y inventory) and stays small negative; the bar is sourced to the company guide plus one estimate source that agrees with it; short interest was checked before the negatives (10% float, not crowded enough to flip them)
